working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass, Kirkistown Castle and Beyond
angle: County Down is home to one of the world's most celebrated links courses, but the real draw for a UK visitor is that you can build a multi-day circuit around it: Royal County Down as the centrepiece, Ardglass for clifftop drama at a fraction of the price, and Kirkistown Castle on the Ards Peninsula for a proper links test that almost nobody outside Northern Ireland talks about. The post treats RCD not as an aspirational fantasy but as a bookable, budget-requiring reality, and gives equal weight to the supporting cast that makes the trip genuinely worth the ferry crossing.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD) Championship Course: Newcastle, County Down. Opened 1889. Designed by Old Tom Morris, later refined by Harry Colt and others. Par 71, 7,186 yards. Sits between the Mourne Mountains and Dundrum Bay/Irish Sea. Consistently ranked in world top 5. Two courses on site: Championship Links and Annesley Links (par 66, 4,617 yards, redesigned by Mackenzie & Ebert in 2015).
- RCD visitor green fees 2026 (from club's own enquiry page): Championship Course £450 (20 April–16 October 2026). Annesley Course £120 same period. Full payment required at booking; non-refundable. All play in four-ball groups; minimum one caddie required per group.
- RCD visitor days: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday (Championship). Advance booking essential; availability limited.
- Belfast City Airport (BHD) is 30–40 minutes from Newcastle by car. Belfast International (BFS) is around 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes away. Ferries run to Belfast from Cairnryan (Scotland) and Liverpool — good entry point for UK visitors avoiding flights.
- From Belfast to Newcastle via the A24: approximately 45 minutes by car.
- Ardglass Golf Club: clifftop links on the south-east County Down coast, established 1896. Par 70, approximately 6,268 yards. The clubhouse occupies a fortified building whose original construction dates to the 15th century (variously described as 14th–15th century in sources — keep general: 'medieval castle'). Irish Sea comes into play on eight holes; sea visible from all 18. About 30 minutes from Royal County Down at Newcastle; roughly an hour from Belfast. Open to visitors. Described as significantly more affordable than RCD — do not invent a specific price as sources conflict.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: Cloughey, Ards Peninsula, County Down. Founded 1902. Present layout by James Braid (1934 visit/modifications). Par 69–70 (sources vary slightly), approximately 6,167 yards. Most easterly 18-hole course in Ireland. Nearest links course to Belfast (about 45 minutes by road). Quick-drying sandy links terrain — rarely closed even after heavy rain. Elevated tees and greens a notable feature. Visitor green fees: from around £35 weekday, £40 weekend (per Golfshake, treat as indicative only — direct club check advised). Visitors welcome seven days a week. Signature hole the par-4 10th.
- Warrenpoint Golf Club: parkland, par 71, 6,173 yards, founded 1893. Overlooks Carlingford Lough with Mourne Mountains backdrop. Visitor weekday green fees from around £38 (per The Stimp — treat as indicative). Good contrast option if the group wants a parkland round. Has hosted Irish Professional Championship and Ladies European Tour events.
- Strangford–Portaferry ferry: short car ferry crossing that links the Lecale Peninsula side (near Ardglass/Downpatrick) with the Ards Peninsula (for Kirkistown). Useful routing tip for golfers doing Ardglass and Kirkistown in one trip — crosses Strangford Lough.
- Slieve Donard Resort & Spa in Newcastle is the obvious high-end base next to RCD. Burrendale Hotel (Newcastle) is a mid-range alternative frequently bundled in golf packages with RCD and Ardglass.
- RCD was founded 1889 and hosted the Walker Cup in 2007; hosted the Irish Open in 2015; consistently ranked among world's top courses including previously being listed number one by Golf Digest outside the US.
- The Open returned to Northern Ireland (Royal Portrush, County Antrim) in 2025 — useful context for why NI golf is in the spotlight for UK visitors right now, without duplicating the Causeway/Portrush angle.
- Post must NOT fabricate specific green fees beyond what's verifiable; for Ardglass and Kirkistown, steer readers to check club websites directly.
